display.purpose: Title-block h1 on every surface; never larger.

label.purpose: Small-caps tracked metadata labels, table headers, field labels. The system's signature voice.

shadows.name: sheet-ambient
shadows.purpose: The only shadow on resting sheets; separates sheet from paper ground.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: Detail-sheet modal lifted over a 45% scrim.

shadows.name: auth-lift
shadows.purpose: Auth sheet on the empty board.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.value: color 0.15s ease, background-color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Secondary Button

components.description: Reserved for destructive confirms only; 7px radius, hover deepens to red-deep.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-danger"><svg class="ds-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18"/></svg>Delete</button>

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Sheet-filled field with an annotation label; blue focus ring, vermillion error.

components.name: Status Text (Blue)
components.description: Published / submitted / active statuses are plain text, not pills or bordered badges.

components.name: Status Text (Red / Late)
components.description: Late / past-due / destructive status. Vermillion appears rarely, and only here.

components.name: Navigation Item
components.description: Drawing-index entry: icon + label, rounded pill, active sheet as a blue wash pill.

components.name: Stat Block
components.description: A measurement note on the sheet: tracked label over a blue-ink tabular figure.

components.name: Ruled Table
components.description: The ruled drawing of every list: uppercase tracked headers, hairline rows, tabular figures, all columns centered.

narrative.overview: This is not a SaaS dashboard — it is an engineering drawing of the assignment cycle. Every screen is read the way a machinist reads a sheet: warm drafting paper as the ground, hairline ink rules separating information, a title block naming each surface, plain-text statuses where any other system would reach for a tinted pill, and engineering-blue as the only active ink. Vermillion appears solely for revision — a late submission, an overdue deadline, a destructive action — because in drafting, red is the color of "change this, this is wrong." The system refuses the generic "white card + rounded shadow" default outright. Cards are sheets: crisp-cornered rectangles with hairline frames and corner registration marks, floating on a faint drafting grid. Tabular numerals everywhere a number appears. Small-caps tracked labels read like drawing annotations. Nothing is ambiguous; a deadline is a dimension, a status is plain text, a list is a ruled table.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with a faint drafting grid; content lives on sheets, never directly on the grid
Hairline rules and crisp corners (3px max); depth by tonal wash, not heavy shadow
Blue = active work; vermillion = revision/late/destructive; green = reviewed/complete; gray = dormant (draft)
Statuses are plain text in cells and cards, never tinted pills or bordered badges
Tabular numerals for all figures; small-caps tracked labels for all field/annotation text
The sidebar is a "drawing index" — a left rail of sheet entries with a blue edge on the active sheet

rules.name: The One-Ink Rule
rules.body: Blue for active work, vermillion for revision/destruction, green for completion, gray for dormant. Each color means exactly one thing; two states never share an ink.

rules.name: The Rarity of Red Rule
rules.body: Vermillion appears on under ~10% of any screen. Its scarcity is what makes a late state alarming.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Every piece of metadata is introduced by a small-caps tracked label, never bare text. If you cannot name the datum, it does not belong on the sheet.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Any number that can be compared — marks, deadlines, counts — uses tabular numerals so columns and totals align.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Sheets are flat at rest. Shadows exist only to separate the modal and the auth sheet from the board; everything else uses tone and hairline.

rules.name: The Blue Wash Rule
rules.body: All hover/active feedback is a blue tonal wash, never a shadow or scale change.

dos: Do open every surface with a title block: name left, action/revision note right, strong hairline below.
Do express statuses as plain text and figures as tabular numerals.
Do keep corners at 3px (2px for icon buttons).
Do use vermillion only for late/overdue/destructive — nothing else.
Do introduce every metadata value with a small-caps annotation label.
Do place all content on sheets; the drafting grid is the ground, never a backdrop behind readable content.
donts: Don't use white cards with rounded-lg-style 8px+ radius, heavy shadows, or gradient fills — the sheet replaces the card.
Don't render statuses as colored pill backgrounds or bordered badges; use plain text.
Don't mix green into constructive buttons or blue into completion states; the One-Ink Rule holds.
Don't let any screen exceed one filled accent color at a time.
Don't add motion to rest states; transitions are brief (0.12–0.15s) color/border fades only.
